requirements.summary: Choose one listed course carrying 3–4 credits, or two listed courses carrying 1.5 credits each. Individual credits are not supplied in this pool; the two selection routes must not be conflated.

requirements.title: University degree GPA and residency
requirements.summary: CWRU cumulative GPA must be at least 2.000. Earn at least 60 CWRU credit hours, including 15 after reaching 105 total credits. At least half of all major requirements, including required related-field courses and major electives, must be completed in CWRU courses.

requirements.title: Catalog choice and extended study
requirements.summary: Use matriculation requirements or elect a later Bulletin. Beyond ten years, the department may update the major and the Associate Provost may update unfinished general education after reviewing the academic record.

requirements.title: BA school requirements
requirements.summary: Earn at least 120 total credit hours, including 90 in arts and sciences and 30 at the 300/400 level. Arts/sciences includes College of Arts and Sciences courses and biochemistry, computer/data sciences, economics, neuroscience and nutrition. Concurrent BA+BS students are exempt from six of the 90 arts/sciences hours. The cumulative average for graded major courses must be at least 2.000.

requirements.title: Unified General Education Requirements
requirements.summary: Applies to matriculants from 2023–2024; earlier cohorts can elect a later Bulletin. A course may fulfill every requirement for which it is approved, except that a cross-listed course counts in only one breadth area. Pools are the complete published Bulletin inventory; later approvals may be added during the year.

requirements.title: Breadth outside AI: arts/humanities and social sciences/management
requirements.summary: AI is classified STEM+N. Earn at least 18 credits with passing letter grades in A+H and SS+M, at least six in each. Up to nine may use approved tests/transfer; at least three credits in each area must be taken at CWRU. Incoming transfer students may receive additional approved pre-matriculation transfer breadth credit. One cross-listed course may count toward only one breadth area.

requirements.title: Communication sequence and Experience Portfolio
requirements.summary: Pass with letter grades an Academic Inquiry Seminar in the first or second semester, two communication-intensive courses of at least three credits each, disciplinary communication of at least three credits, and a capstone of at least three credits. requirements.title: Quantitative and perspectives credit policies

Moral/ethical reasoning, global perspectives, and human diversity each require passing letter grades in an approved course or sequence. Local/global engagement permits passing an approved course/sequence or participating in an approved activity. Transfer substitution for any perspective requires FSCUE appeal approval.

requirements.title: Secondary-major relationship
requirements.summary: This record represents the full AI degree. Students completing AI only as a secondary major within another undergraduate degree are exempt from this AI degree's school-specific requirements under the published program policy.

requirements.title: Conditional requisite and career permission
requirements.summary: Course prerequisites, corequisites and other enrollment conditions remain binding unless Requisites Not Met permission is granted. Cross-career restrictions can additionally require approval from the student’s or course’s school registrar/dean. Listed graduate-program-restricted electives such as SCMG 462/463 are conditional options requiring the relevant permissions if the student does not meet their published conditions. Listing is not guaranteed enrollment or blanket waiver; after approval the student must still register.

requirements.title: Career permission requires administrator action
requirements.summary: Career-restricted enrollment requests require action by the appropriate school registrar or administrator in addition to any instructor action. Permission can be granted or denied; approval does not itself enroll the student.
